svg.title: A good plan makes room for people

text.tspan: People work together in a shared space.
A good plan makes room for people
A good collaborative plan should provide direction while leaving room for change. Preparing a small exhibition at our
neighbourhood library taught us that shared priorities and practical testing make this balance possible.
First, agreeing on constraints gives a team a useful starting point. With a narrow room and a modest budget, we
mapped out the visitor’s journey before choosing displays. This shared reference point helped us decide which ideas
Second, testing a plan makes flexibility practical. Our trial run revealed that the entrance would become crowded. We
moved the introductory panel further inside, solving the problem before it required a costly last-minute change.
Effective coordination therefore combines clear priorities with opportunities to adjust. By making decisions visible and
checking in before the deadline, a team can remain organised without becoming rigid. That is what makes a plan
BUILD YOUR OWN · Thesis: direction plus flexibility. Body 1: shared priorities, with a planning example. Body 2: testing, with
a revision example. Conclude by connecting both. Follow the main idea through two supported points. The conclusion brings
both points together without adding a new reason.
What did the trial run reveal, and how did the team respond? (Model: It revealed that the entrance would become crowded.
The team moved the introductory panel further inside.)
